Commentary.Commentary: Zimbabwe, on the other hand, had no clues to the onslaught by Rahim and Mominul. They were bowling it here and there, conceding easy runs to the Bangla batters and now the batters have a tough job on their hands. Ainsley Ndlovu bowled well while others were very disappointing. They were bolwing negative lines and lengths, which was not even enough to trouble the batters. Now they have to bat and bat as long as possible to have any chances of a draw. There is rain predicted for the fourth and fifth day. Surely Zimbabwe will hope that the predictions come true. Join us in a while for the third innings.

Rahim has declared immediately after getting to his double-century. It ends a brilliant innings for Bangladesh and they have got a lead of 295 runs. Bangladesh lost an early wicket in the form of Saif Hassan and then Tamim Iqbal along with Najmul Hossain Shanto steadied things up. Once they fell, it was the partnership between Mominul Haque and Mushfiqur Rahim that defined the innings. They stitched a 222-run partnership and once Mominul Haque fell after his century, it was Das and Rahim who did the damage. They took the lead to above 250 and when Rahim reached his 3rd double ton, they eventually declared.

... Day 3, Session 3 ...

In the final session of Day 3, Bangladesh would look to keep on batting while Zimbabwe would hope to pick up the remaining wickets as quickly as possible. Will we see a fightback from Zimbabwe? Join us at 1430 Local (0830 GMT) for the final session.

Zimbabwe, on the other hand, would feel slightly better with the two wickets that they managed to pick up in this session but they would know that they are way behind in this game and they need to pick the remaining wickets quickly if they do not want Bangladesh to run away with the game, if that has not happened already. Ainsley Ndlovu was the pick of the bowlers scalping two wickets but the others were disappointing.

A better session for Zimbabwe but Bangladesh still hold the cards in this Test match. Rahim and Mominul started the session positively and were going good till Ndlovu removed the Bangladesh skipper with a terrific return catch. Then Mithun looked good for his short stint but Ndlovu struck to remove them but since then Das and Rahim have played out the remaining overs with ease, with the latter looking set to reach his 150. They scored 91 runs in 28 overs and have swelled up their lead to 177.

Hello and welcome to the coverage of the one-off Test between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe. Bangladesh batted superbly on Day 2 to get the deficit down to just 25 runs and the three 50-plus stands for the hosts deflated the visitors. Skipper Mominul Haque is still out there and he has Mushfiqur Rahim for company. Both these batsmen will first look to wipe out the deficit without any further damage and then would want to bat long to push Zimbabwe out of the game. The visitors were decent with the ball the other day but were deprived of wickets on a regular basis. A fresh day to begin with and they would want to take quick wickets to dry up the run flow. Earlier in the day, Bangladesh bowlers took just over an hour to wrap things up in the morning, with Abu Jayed and Nayeem Hasan taking 4 wickets apiece. Both bowled really well, with Jayed moving the ball in the air while Nayeem making it spin off the deck.

A near perfect batting day for Bangladesh. Yes, 3 batsmen in the top 4 wasted their starts but it can also be viewed as 4 batsmen in the top 5 crossed the 30-mark and faced more than 50 balls. They spent time in the middle and then started to accumulate runs quickly.

Not a great outing with the ball for the visitors. They started well, got the early wicket but then were subjected to 3 successive 50-plus stands. There was barely any movement or swing for the seamers while the spinners struggled for turn. A quality spinner is being missed, which can be seen by the fact that Sikandar Raza had to bowl 22 overs.

120/1 in 33 overs in that final session. Bangladesh have really pressed it in, pushing Zimbabwe on the mat. The first two sessions did feel as if Zimbabwe did have some sort of a chance if quick wickets fell but the Mominul-Rahim stand has almost shut the door.
